Supreme Judicial Court of Massachusetts, 1942. 
311 Mass. 677, 42 N.E.2d 808.

There is no allegation of any false statement or representation, or of

at arm's length. The charge is concealment and nothing more; and it is 
concealment in the simple sense of mere failure to reveal. with nothing 
to show any peculiar duty to speak. The characterization 
of the 
concealment as false and fraudulent of course adds nothing in the 
absence of further 
allegations of fact. Province Securities 
Corp. v. 
Maryland Casualty Co., 269 Mass. 75, 92, 168 S.E. 252.
